This @ncte EJ piece is special to me for many reasons: 

1) it was my 1st collaboration w/#hfellows @TchKimPossible & #pawlp @DrPSchmidt

2) it emerged from a dynamic & rich #TeachHateUGive chat last year

3) and most importantly, bc #WeNeedDiverseBooks & #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/vwLRCb2MaM

@DulceFlecha I ended up really liking it! If you like audiobooks, this one is pretty good to listen to. She has a great essay at the end of the book that also explains her rationale for writing the novel and connects it to #BlackLivesMatter and other social issues.

A3. Could the text be used to interrogate sexism & #metoo? Abigail is framed as the villain yet Proctor—“the hero”—could use his power to take advantage. Does the text perpetuate stereotypes of women as manipulative, their accusations not to be believed? #DisruptTexts https://t.co/UfH8Dbjrjg
